summary.name: Whispering
summary.one_liner: Whispering is an open-source speech-to-text app that transcribes audio using either cloud providers (Groq, OpenAI, ElevenLabs) or a local model via Speaches.
use_cases: Dictating text into any application with a keyboard shortcut
Transcribing audio locally without sending data to servers
Transcribing speech using cheap cloud APIs with your own key
Cleaning up or reformatting transcribed text with AI workflows
Processing recordings made in a separate recording app
summary.what_it_does: Whispering records speech when you press a shortcut and inserts the resulting text wherever your cursor is on the system. It supports cloud transcription through Groq (Distil and Large models), OpenAI Whisper, and ElevenLabs, using your own API keys so audio goes directly to the provider. It can also run fully local transcription through Speaches. The app can format text, fix grammar, and run custom AI workflows on the output. The page says local storage is used and there are no middleman servers.
notable: Choice of cloud providers (Groq, OpenAI, ElevenLabs) or fully local transcription with Speaches
Audio goes directly to providers via your own API key; no middleman servers
Listed as open source and freeware in awesome-mac
caveats: Optimized for quick transcriptions; the page recommends a dedicated recording app for long sessions
Native builds listed: Apple Silicon only on macOS, Windows 10/11 and all distributions for Linux are named, plus browser access
Subscription row in the pricing table ($10-30/month) is not explained on the page
